_comment: ENUM-PARITY BASELINE. Read by tests/enum-parity.test.ts. One number per service: the maximum
count of DISTINCT Zod enum sites that no PHP enum resolves to, by rule key, manual bridge or
class name. IT MAY ONLY SHRINK. The gate prints the new number the moment it falls, and fails
when it rises, exactly like ratchet.json and the allow-lists next to it. Never raise it to turn
a red suite green: an unmapped enum is a value list we promise an agent and compare to nothing.
Distinct SITES, not occurrences: one shared value object reached from 99 tools is one unpinned
promise and one edit, and counting it 99 times would make the number a popularity contest.
What is in the count today, by class (run pnpm test to print the full list with an owning tool):
1. CreditsSpentValue.reason / .executed_on, on every creditable action envelope in all three
services. Core\Values\CreditsSpentValue::validate() constrains them with Rule::in over CLASS
CONSTANTS, not an enum, so no enum dump can ever carry them and no name can reach them. Clears
only by promoting those constants to a real enum in gtm.lib.common.
2. sort.field / sort.direction / include.* / group_by on searches whose FormRequest constrains
none of them. gtm.service.id resolves nearly all of these positionally because its search
requests carry Rule::in; most linkedin and orchestration ones declare 'nullable' only, so our
Zod enum is STRICTER than the backend rather than drifting from it. Clears one FormRequest at
3. Four singles with no PHP enum behind them at all: the latest-engine refresh stop_reason, the
webhook test-send error_kind, the recommendations direction and the notifications group_by.
